literal: The good path that which is called if you ask what, it is the path that embraces the non-killing of any single thing.
translation: If you ask what is called the good path, it is the path that embraces the non-killing of any living thing whatsoever.
modern: நல்ல வழி என்று சொல்லப்படுவது எதுவென்றால், எந்த ஒரு உயிரையும் கொல்லாத அறவழியைப் பின்பற்றுவதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate path of virtue by posing a direct question and answering it. The 'good path' (nallāṟu) is identified as the path of non-killing (kollāmai). The phrase 'yātonṟum' emphasizes that this applies to absolutely any living creature, without exception. The word 'sūḻum' suggests actively embracing, protecting, or constantly pursuing this principle, showing that true virtue lies in the conscious preservation of all life.
